messages:
jun: heads-up — last hour we had 6 Xid/ECC errors across the us-west GPU pool. tensor-serving retried 3 workloads.
ops-bot: [ALERT] GPU-ECC-Threshold exceeded on node-gpu-112 (us-west-2). count=4 in 10m
sarah: logs? dmesg / journalctl + nvidia-smi output available?
jun: yes — but they're fragmented across node journals. we need a normalized collector: always snapshot last 256 lines of dmesg, `journalctl -k -n 300 --no-pager`, and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid,serial,name,driver_version,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv,noheader,nounits` on alert.
matt: agree. also capture `nvidia-smi -q -x` when possible (xml) for retired pages + ECC counters. store as structured fields: node, gpu_index, uuid, timestamp, raw_dmesg, kernel_logs, nvidia_summary
ana: sample parser approach: don't rely on brittle regexes. extract event keys (Xid code, ECC uncorrected, "GPU has fallen off the bus", retired pages) and compute a canonical signature hash for indexing.
jun: quick collector snippet to start from (bash):
```bash
# collect snapshot
DMESG=$(dmesg | tail -n 256)
KLOG=$(journalctl -k -n 300 --no-pager)
NSMI=$(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid,serial,name,driver_version,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile --format=csv,noheader,nounits)
# emit json (requires jq)
jq -n --arg node "$NODE" --arg dm "$DMESG" --arg klog "$KLOG" --arg nsmi "$NSMI" '{node:$node,dm:$dm,klog:$klog,nsmi:$nsmi,timestamp:(now|tostring)}'
```

sarah: perfect. retention/cost question: can we avoid keeping raw dmesg forever?
jun: plan: keep raw snapshots for 7d (zstd compressed), keep parsed events and signatures indexed indefinitely. if node is healthy for 30d, purge raw payloads older than 7d.
matt: add a small metric export: gpu_error_events_total{reason="xid|ecc|bus|retired"} with last_seen and count; make alert rules use that.
nana: also include mapping table uuid -> machine serial + rack/region label in each message for fast cross-search. avoid free-text hostnames.
diego: ops flow proposal: on alert -> collector runs -> parser returns canonical event + severity. if severity >= major (uncorrected ECC or Xid FATAL) -> set node annotation `gpu.health=unhealthy` and `kubectl taint nodes <node> gpu=drain:NoSchedule` -> create infra ticket with collector payload attached.
sarah: can we auto-drain after 2 fatal events in 1h for non-prod?
jun: yes. for prod require manual approval. we can implement a policy switch per node-pool.
ops-bot: action created: INFRA-823 implement_normalized_gpu_loghook (assignee: jun)
matt: i'll open a PR in loghook repo with parser rules and add unit tests for Xid/ECC extraction.
nana: i'll update the oncall runbook with retention policy + auto-drain thresholds and add playbook steps to reassign workloads.
sarah: deployment plan?
jun: PR -> canary on staging GPUs (24h) -> roll to us-west non-prod -> monitor 48h -> prod. rollback on >50% increase in job retries.
all: :thumbsup:
